title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Followup
summary: Weeky POC sync focused on the Apr 10 reliability incident (timeouts, 5xx spikes, and rate-limiting). transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM), Jenna Ortiz (NimbleHealth Eng Mgr), Marcus Liu (NimbleHealth SRE), Priya Kapoor (NimbleHealth Product), Tom Becker (NimbleHealth Platform)

Summary (auto): follow up on the Apr 10 incident that caused 5xx spikes and timeouts during peak POC traffic; review mitigations and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, real quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Jenna: Jenna here.
[00:00:14] Marcus: Marcus on SRE.
[00:00:16] Priya: Priya, product.
[00:00:18] Tom: Tom, platform.
[00:00:20] Samir: Samir, SE at Redwood.
[00:00:22] Avery: Great, Lina from CSM is here as well. Alright, agenda — quick incident recap, what we learned, mitigations we already applied, and decide the next controlled test.
[00:00:35] Jenna: Sounds good. Marcus can you kick us off with the timeline from your side?
[00:00:40] Marcus: Yeah — on Apr 10 around 20:00 UTC we saw a spike of 5xxs, predominantly 504 gateway timeouts and some 503 service unavailables. The spike correlated with a burst in prefix-miss requests, so KV cache miss rate jumped. We also saw pod restarts from the autoscaler during the window. CPU wasn't fully saturated but tail latencies increased.
[00:01:05] Samir: When you say prefix-miss, do you mean cache misses at the runtime layer or upstream?
[00:01:10] Marcus: Runtime KV cache — most requests that hit long context lengths didn't get KV warm so memory pressure plus slightly higher OOM retry churn. Also client retry behavior seemed aggressive: several clients retrying every 200ms which created a retry storm on top of the cold-cache latencies.
[00:01:32] Avery: Ok that fits our initial telemetry — we saw a short burst of 429s and 5xxs in our gateway logs. There was a momentary autoscaler thrash when a new node group spun up, and because the KV cache is per-instance the first few requests to those instances were expensive.
[00:01:48] Jenna: Do you think the autoscaler caused the 5xxs or was it just exposing the cache problem?
[00:01:54] Samir: Prob both — autoscaler created capacity but those new replicas were cold and couldn't serve the heavy context quickly. Combined with aggressive client retries and no circuit breaker, the new replicas got hammered and returned 504s while they bootstrapped.
[00:02:10] Marcus: We also have an ingress timeout at 30s, some of the requests hit that after repeated retries.
[00:02:15] Priya: Sorry to interrupt, quick Q — what about the model variant? Were you on a larger model for that window?
[00:02:20] Avery: Good point — during that test we were using rdx-13b-int8 as primary, with rdx-6b as fallback. There was some fallback traffic but not enough to absorb the burst.
[00:02:31] Tom: From platform side we saw client-side retries coming from two internal services that had default 100ms retry backoff. We think a couple of them were misconfigured after the rollout.
[00:02:45] Samir: So we recommended immediate mitigations: 1) client-side backoff increase and randomized jitter, 2) temporary rate cap per IP/route at the gateway, 3) enable model fallback aggressively for poorly performing instances, and 4) short-term disable scale-to-zero so pods remain warm during critical windows.
[00:03:05] Jenna: Which of those do we already enable?
[00:03:08] Avery: You already put in the temporary rate cap on Apr 11, and Marcus increased client backoff in the most aggressive caller. We also set a conservative pod min-replicas to avoid scale-to-zero during peak.
[00:03:21] Marcus: Yes, those changes dropped the 5xx rate by roughly 70% in subsequent runs, but we still saw occasional 504s under very bursty synthetic traffic.
[00:03:31] Priya: Is there a way to detect retry storms and pause incoming traffic before hitting the model?
[00:03:36] Samir: We can add a circuit-breaker at the edge that trips based on error rate or latency. We also support token-bucket rate limiting and per-route quotas. For detection, our tracing shows request fan-out and repeated request IDs; if you can surface the request IDs we can correlate and detect duplicates server-side.
[00:03:58] Tom: Marcus can we change the client to send a request-id header?
[00:04:01] Marcus: Yep we can do that. We'll add unique request ids and forward them.
[00:04:05] Avery: Great — that will help dedupe and make root cause clearer.
[00:04:08] Jenna: On the autoscaler note, is there a recommended config so the scale doesn't thrash in these scenarios?
[00:04:14] Samir: We recommend smoothing with a higher scale-up cooldown and using proactive warm pools for the most latency-sensitive routes. Also prefer vertical buffer (more memory) rather than spinning many small instances if your workload has heavy KV dependencies.
[00:04:30] Priya: What's the quick lift to get dedupe and circuit-breaker in place?
[00:04:34] Samir: Circuit-breaker is a config change on the gateway we can push; dedupe needs client request id addition. Both are low-to-medium effort. We can ship the CB in a day for the pilot.
[00:04:45] Marcus: For logs, I exported kube events and our ingress logs for Apr 10; I'll share a trimmed set. There are a few stack traces from the runtime showing a transient memory spike on those new pods.
[00:04:58] Avery: Please include the pprof traces if possible — that helps us see where time's spent during those long tails.
[00:05:02] Marcus: Will do.
[00:05:05] Samir: One more note — we saw some 502s that looked like upstream TLS handshakes failing briefly when the node rotated. That's likely a keepalive/connection pool configuration gap.
[00:05:17] Tom: We can increase keepalive and also tune connection pools.
[00:05:21] Priya: Any impact on data privacy or logs we should be careful about sharing?
[00:05:25] Lina: We have the standard NDA in place; we're only asking for trimmed logs with PII masked. We'll provide an S3 upload with a presigned link.
[00:05:35] Jenna: Ok — let's talk about longer-term fixes. Is there a pattern we should watch for in production?
[00:05:40] Samir: Watch cache miss rate, tail latency, number of cold replicas, and retry amplification. Also our latency percentiles at the model runtime layer (p95/p99) and the error budget consumed per hour.
[00:05:53] Marcus: Can Redwood provide a dashboard we can add to our Pager duty runbook?
[00:05:57] Avery: Yes, we'll share a read-only dashboard link (we have a template).
[00:06:02] Samir: Also, for the POC we can add a short-term config: aggressive fallback to rdx-6b under excessive tail latency, plus prefix caching for common prompts so the KV warms faster.
[00:06:15] Jenna: How does aggressive fallback affect cost and quality?
[00:06:20] Avery: Fallback reduces cost per token but may change output quality slightly. For transactional endpoints where correctness matters, we can fallback only for non-critical routes. For exploratory features it's a good safety valve.
[00:06:33] Priya: We want to avoid user-visible regression. Can we A/B test fallback?
[00:06:37] Samir: Absolutely — Redwood supports canary rollouts and split traffic for gradual fallback testing.
[00:06:44] Tom: On rate limits, do you throttle per route or per account?
[00:06:49] Samir: Both. We can do per-route, per-api-key, and per-ip policies. For the pilot we recommended a per-route cap with a burst allowance.
[00:06:58] Marcus: Quick question — the 5xxs, were they real server errors or client connection issues?
[00:07:03] Samir: Mixed — some were genuine runtime timeouts (model execution exceeding ingress timeout), some were 502/503 from connection pool exhaustion, and some were autoretries from ephemeral OOMs.
[00:07:15] Jenna: Ok — sounds like we need a combined plan: client backoff + dedupe + circuit breaker + dashboard + controlled load test.
[00:07:23] Avery: Agreed. For the controlled test, Samir can run a bench with different traffic shapes and we can instrument the run. We should include a bursty pattern to reproduce the issue and a steady-state run to ensure no regressions.
[00:07:36] Samir: I'll also try a version where we pre-warm KV caches and compare tail latency.
[00:07:41] Priya: How long do pre-warms take?
[00:07:44] Samir: Depends on model context size and the number of replicas; typically a few seconds per replica to warm high-frequency prefixes, but full warm might be longer if you need a large prefix set. We have tooling to seed the cache ahead of time.
[00:07:58] Marcus: For the Apr 10 incident, can you annotate where the retries amplified?
[00:08:02] Avery: We added markers in the logs where we saw incoming retry loops — you'll see request count per request-id spike. Marcus, if you share the request-ids we can map them.
[00:08:11] Marcus: Yes, will export those.
[00:08:14] Jenna: Any other blockers from Redwood side?
[00:08:16] Samir: No blockers; just need the logs and a window for the controlled test. We'll also share a proposed circuit-breaker config and rate-cap values.
[00:08:26] Tom: For rate cap values, what's a safe starting point?
[00:08:29] Samir: Start with 10 rps per api-key with a burst of 50, then tune upward based on tail latency. For heavy batchers we can open a higher path with batching.
[00:08:40] Priya: One operational ask — can we have alerting on 5xx spike >5% in a 5 min window?
[00:08:45] Lina: We can set that up in the shared dashboard and create an ops playbook.
[00:08:50] Marcus: Also, we want to verify the autoscaler cooldown changes. I'll push a config change to increase scale-up cooldown to 90s and keep min-replicas at 3 for peak windows.
[00:09:01] Samir: That should help.
[00:09:03] Jenna: Ok quick recap of owners?
[00:09:06] Avery: Marcus - logs and request ids by Apr 16.
[00:09:09] Marcus: Yep.
[00:09:11] Avery: Samir - bench plan and circuit-breaker config by Apr 20.
[00:09:14] Samir: On it.
[00:09:15] Avery: I'll share the trimmed logs link and the read-only dashboard once I have them.
[00:09:19] Avery: Any final questions?
[00:09:21] Priya: One quick one — are there any known runtime patches we should be on the lookout for?
[00:09:26] Samir: We shipped a small fix for connection pooling last week that reduces TLS handshake failures; it's in staging and we'll push to pilot after we finish the bench.
[00:09:36] Tom: Good.
[00:09:38] Jenna: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[00:09:40] Avery: Thanks all. We'll follow up in writing — next sync after the controlled bench run unless something urgent comes up.
[00:09:48] End of transcript.
